title: Tooling: 2.09x faster exact single-intersection Gram replay
head: f015b04c74801fa330f818d178e809c760fb5469
body:
The historical single-intersection audit spends most of its runtime constructing exact binary Gram matrices. This replaces repeated large-integer sums with symmetric byte packing, preserving every matrix entry and every basis, closure, rank, and rejection check. **Tooling improvement; no new κ.**

Three alternating fresh-process pairs on CPython 3.13.1 / macOS arm64 measured median complete-audit time **13.766 → 6.597 seconds (2.087× faster)**. Median peak process RSS rises from **49,266,688 to 68,845,568 bytes (about 40%)**; this is an explicit speed/memory tradeoff. Every sample and source pin is retained in `research/single-intersection-packing/RESULT.json`.

Validation:

- Compare all **100,203,737 entries** of the four committed orbit Gram matrices against an unmodified, hash-pinned predecessor implementation.
- Every timed run recomputes all **5,257 historical screen cases**, basis independence, adjacent-transposition closure, and exact Gram ranks. The complete certificate has its original SHA256 after restoring only the changed implementation-source binding.
- **16 focused tests pass normally and under `-O`**, including source corruption, changed certificate ranks/rows/bindings, a wrong matrix entry, malformed labels, dependent bases, missing closure, byte boundaries, permutations, and large labels.
- Both affected certificate producers pass. `single-intersection.json` and `affine-vector-screens.json` change only their implementation-source hashes; complete predecessor-certificate equivalence is regression-tested.
- `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 make verify-tests`: **557 tests in 86 isolated modules and 20 patch checks pass**. Selected-record integrity and whitespace checks also pass.

Reproduce with standard-library Python 3.11+ on macOS or Linux, using a fresh output path:

```sh
python3 -B research/single-intersection-packing/benchmark.py --rounds 3 --output /tmp/single-intersection-packing.json
```

Expected: `PASS_IDENTICAL_GRAM_ROWS_AND_COMPLETE_CERTIFICATES`. Timing is descriptive, not a pass threshold. The engineering note at `docs/research/single-intersection-packing.md` explains the packing identity, complete coverage, measured tradeoff, and commands.

Base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`. OS-random seed **86**, verification engineering. Candidates were gather schedules, coded-carry controls, and single-intersection replay; seed 86 mod 3 selected the latter. Profiling justified narrowing the initial feature-reuse hypothesis to Gram construction. There was no sprint coordination issue, so the claim is local. Overlap checks covered 594 open PRs through #775; #707 concerns R420 determinant prefixes and #756 balanced-Fano search. Neither supplies code here.

Credit Douglas R. Colkitt's preserved single-intersection audit and its cited mathematical sources. Contribution by **merramil with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance**, under Apache-2.0; `NOTICE.md` identifies the exact predecessor and source hash.

`upstream/` and the selected frontier are unchanged. Full `make verify`, selected-supplier cold replay, and Lean were not rerun for this historical-checker change. All inherited construction, compiler, hosting, precision, tape, and analytic assumptions remain. This is finite verification tooling, not a formal proof of the multiplication theorem.
limits: Metadata and source identity only. Checks require source/command/coverage review; no green-badge inference.
